questions.prompt: Why does x² - (2 + i)x = 0 have the solution 2 + i but not the solution 2 - i?
questions.prompt_markup: Why does x² - (2 + i)x = 0 have the solution 2 + i but not the solution 2 - i?

choices.text: Substituting 2 - i gives (2 - i)² - (2 + i)(2 - i) = 0, so 2 - i is a solution after all.
Non-real solutions of every quadratic equation come in conjugate pairs, so 2 - i must also be a solution, along with 2 + i.
Its coefficient 2 + i is not real, so its solutions need not come in conjugate pairs; factoring x(x - (2 + i)) = 0 gives only 0 and 2 + i.
A quadratic equation can have only one non-real solution, so once 2 + i is found there is no room for 2 - i.

questions.correct_answer: Its coefficient 2 + i is not real, so its solutions need not come in conjugate pairs; factoring x(x - (2 + i)) = 0 gives only 0 and 2 + i.
questions.grading_note: The conjugate-pair rule needs real coefficients. The others apply the rule without that condition, misstate the number of solutions, or miscompute: (2 - i)² - (2 + i)(2 - i) = 3 - 4i - 5 ≠ 0.
